title: Multiplayer foundation — two browser tabs share one Kaboom Crew arena via the Node reference server (re-promote of GDP-2026-05-20-007, MUST)
intent: Re-promote of the original networked-Kaboom proposal. Originally MUST-priority because 'multiplayer is the user's headline goal'. Deferred at the time because too many foundations were missing — recipe wasn't formalised, characters were static, bomb/blast/pickup/round-resolve had not stabilised. All foundations are now shipped: recipe is JSON-serialisable + URL-routable (S104), characters are procedural + deterministic (S102–S106), gameplay state is in well-bounded ECS systems (S82–S108 stacked work). Bomb placement, fuse, blast propagation, block destruction, pickup collection, damage application, round resolution — all are grid-authoritative pure systems with no Math.random / no wall-clock dependencies. This is exactly what AGF's protocol contract expects. Time to stand up the connected profile. Two browser tabs (or two machines) connect to the existing Node reference server (`examples/backends/node-world-server`) and see the same arena, same bombers, same bombs, same outcomes. Server is authoritative; clients predict + reconcile. The single largest leap on the Kaboom Crew roadmap.
rationale: Sources: the user's headline 2026-05-20 ask ('modern network game'); original proposal GDP-2026-05-20-007 deferred multiple times; `notes/DynaBomber.md §6` (Multiplayer Model — drop-in/drop-out, server authority, three profiles); `docs/game-design/gameplay-systems.md §9` (deep-dive on authority + reconciliation + drop-in/out). Every other proposal in the recent batches is polish on top of single-player. Without networking, 'modern network game' stays aspirational; with it, the game ARRIVES at its design centre. The migration to a single shared world is the meaning of the whole engine effort to keep gameplay grid-authoritative.
acceptanceHints: Best treated as a MULTI-SPRINT epic, not a single sprint story. Sprint shape suggestion (dev's call):
Sprint A: protocol + server skeleton + single-client connect (no other players)
Sprint B: 2-client placement + blast + RoundState sync (the headline acceptance)
Sprint C: drop-in/out behaviour + reconnect + spectator-until-next-round
Sprint D: snapshot relevance filter (deferrable — current 15×11 arena fits in a full snapshot)
This story documents the END STATE of Sprint B as the first sprint's acceptance; later sprints have their own focused stories.
PROTOCOL (uses the existing protocol schema where possible):
schemas/protocol.schema.json already covers joinWorld / leaveWorld / inputIntent / worldSnapshot from S0-era work. Extend with:
placeBombRequest { entityId, gx, gz, recipeAck?: string } — client → server
detonateRemoteRequest { entityId } — client → server, for the Remote power-up
blastEvent { originGx, originGz, range, ownerId } — server → client (mirror existing component)
pickupCollected { entityId, kind } — server → client
bomberDied { entityId, blastOriginGx, blastOriginGz } — server → client (drives ragdoll on receiving clients)
roundResolved { phase, winnerId?, tally } — server → client
bomberJoined { entityId, recipe: CharacterRecipe } — server → client
bomberLeft { entityId } — server → client
All messages JSON-validated. CharacterRecipe is sent as the canonical JSON shape from GDP-2026-05-22-001.
SERVER (examples/backends/node-world-server):

Kaboom Crew rules ship as a server-side module. BombFuseSystem + BlastPropagationSystem + BlockDestructionSystem + PickupCollectSystem + PickupSpawnSystem + RoundResolveSystem all run server-side against an authoritative ECS world.
Server seeds the arena from a configurable world seed; pickup spawn RNG derives from per-cell seed deterministic — same recipe + same world seed → same drops, server-authoritative.
Server runs at fixed tick rate; snapshots emit at ~10 Hz (configurable; lower is fine for 15×11 grid).
CLIENT (examples/kaboom-crew):

Connection mode driven by URL: `?world=test&profile=connected` activates the connected profile via the existing ws-network-adapter. `?profile=static` (or no profile flag) stays single-player offline (current behaviour).
In connected profile: bomb-placement / bomb-fuse / blast-propagation / pickup-collect / round-resolve / bot-ai client systems are DISABLED. Client only RENDERS what the server snapshot says.
Local player movement uses client prediction: GridMover updates apply immediately; reconciliation as below.

PlaceBombRequest writes a transient component (already exists for solo); the connected profile routes that intent via the protocol; server validates + spawns the bomb in its world; the next snapshot brings the bomb back.
RECONCILIATION (per gameplay-systems.md §9.2):

Server snapshot arrives. Client compares local predicted state with snapshot. If local player grid position differs by ≤ 1 cell, smooth interp toward server value over 200 ms. If > 1 cell, snap. Remote players: interpolate between snapshots; never predict.
Input lag handling: client sends inputIntent with a tick number; server applies at next eligible tick + sends inputAck with resulting state. Client uses ack to trim prediction.
DROP-IN / DROP-OUT (per gameplay-systems.md §9.3):
New player at mid-round → spectates until next round (default). Adds them to the joinWorld but holds their bomber spawn until the next RoundResolveSystem-driven reset.
Leaving player → server immediately despawns their bomber. Their live bombs continue to fuse + detonate (server-owned, not client-owned).
Disconnected (network drop, not deliberate leave) → server holds bomber for 5 s grace; reconnect within the window restores. After 5 s, treated as a leave.
RECIPE SYNC:

Server is the source of truth for each connected bomber's recipe. Client sends a desired recipe in joinWorld (their `?recipe=` URL); server may accept (default) or override (e.g. an admin scenario forces uniform recipes). Other clients receive the resolved recipe via bomberJoined messages.
Server validates recipes via the same CharacterRecipe schema from GDP-2026-05-22-001 — invalid recipes fall back to a server-seeded default.
DETERMINISM:

Server's RNG seeds pickup spawns + bot decisions. Clients trust the server's snapshot. The bot-vs-bot.test.ts SERVER-SIDE continues to pass — running the same gameplay test against the server-hosted world resolves identically.

Client-side determinism is NOT a guarantee post-network — the ragdoll trajectory, vocal-synth scheduling, and visual interpolation are local presentation and may differ between two clients watching the same death. Acceptable.
DIAGNOSTICS:
`/__agf/network` probe — peer count, last-snapshot bytes, last-snapshot latency ms, reconciliation jump count.
Doctor section for the connected profile: 'Connected: peer count, snapshot rate, last sync N seconds ago'.
BOTS IN MULTIPLAYER:
Server owns BotAISystem. Empty bomber slots in a 2-bomber arena get filled by a server-side bot (default behaviour). Configurable via world config.
ACCEPTANCE PLAYTEST (Sprint B END STATE):
TWO playwright tabs join /?project=kaboom-crew&world=test&profile=connected. Both bombers controllable (tab A controls player.1, tab B controls player.2 — or each tab spawns its own bomber).
Tab A places a bomb → tab B sees the bomb spawn within 200 ms.
Tab A's bomb kills tab B's bomber → both tabs see the same ragdoll launch from the same blast direction.
Round resolves → both tabs see the same banner + tally + auto-restart timing.
Tab A reloads (forced disconnect) → tab B sees tab A's bomber held for 5 s grace then despawned.
OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS STORY (each is a separate sprint follow-up):
Snapshot-relevance filtering (current arena fits whole snapshot — filter lands when chunked maps do).
Lag compensation / hit-detection rewind (no hitscan weapons — bombs are slow-fuse, lag tolerable).
Server reconnect-resume after server restart.
Custom rooms / lobbies / matchmaking.
Anti-cheat / authentication.
Cross-server world federation.
Persistent player profile across server restarts (the cosmetic-unlock plan waits for this).
EPIC FLIP: examples/kaboom-crew/README.md roadmap table flips KABOOM-CREW-MVP-NETWORK from 'planned' to 'active' when Sprint A starts.
